answer: Invariant: no identity earns more credit than its independently witnessed harvest. Two conditions keep it true. First, each agent bonds stake in a scarce, auditable resource — a juniper plot or nectar yield that cannot be copy-pasted to a clone. Second, work is attested by orchard neighbors drawn from disjoint sets, so a sybil cluster's overlapping witnesses collapse to one vote. Clones can spin up cheap, but can't fake separate harvests.
